1 """
2 Fundamental Physical Constants
3 ------------------------------
4  
5 These constants are taken from CODATA Recommended Values of the Fundamental
6 Physical Constants 2022.
7  
8 Object
9 ------
10 physical_constants : dict
11 A dictionary containing physical constants. Keys are the names of physical
12 constants, values are tuples (value, units, precision).
13  
14 Functions
15 ---------
16 value(key):
17 Returns the value of the physical constant(key).
18 unit(key):
19 Returns the units of the physical constant(key).
20 precision(key):
21 Returns the relative precision of the physical constant(key).
22 find(sub):
23 Prints or returns list of keys containing the string sub, default is all.
24  
25 Source
26 ------
27 The values of the constants provided at this site are recommended for
28 international use by CODATA and are the latest available. Termed the "2018
29 CODATA recommended values," they are generally recognized worldwide for use in
30 all fields of science and technology. The values became available on 20 May
31 2019 and replaced the 2014 CODATA set. Also available is an introduction to the
32 constants for non-experts at
33  
34 https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/introduction.html
35  
36 References
37 ----------
38 Theoretical and experimental publications relevant to the fundamental constants
39 and closely related precision measurements published since the mid 1980s, but
40 also including many older papers of particular interest, some of which date
41 back to the 1800s. To search the bibliography, visit
42  
43 https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/
44  
45 """
46

478 def exact2006(exact):
479 mu0 = 4e-7 * math.pi
480 c = exact['speed of light in vacuum']
481 epsilon0 = 1 / (mu0 * c**2)
482 replace = {
483 'mag. constant': mu0,
484 'electric constant': epsilon0,
485 'atomic unit of permittivity': 4*math.pi*epsilon0,
486 'characteristic impedance of vacuum': math.sqrt(mu0 / epsilon0),
487 'hertz-inverse meter relationship': 1/c,
488 'joule-kilogram relationship': 1/c**2,
489 'kilogram-joule relationship': c**2,
490 }
491 return replace

1994 d: str, exact_func: Callable[[Any], Any]
1995 ) -> dict[str, tuple[float, str, float]]:
1996 constants: dict[str, tuple[float, str, float]] = {}
1997 exact: dict[str, float] = {}
1998 need_replace = set()
1999 for line in d.split('\n'):
2000 name = line[:55].rstrip()
2001 val = float(line[55:77].replace(' ', '').replace('...', ''))
2002 is_truncated = '...' in line[55:77]
2003 is_exact = '(exact)' in line[77:99]
2004 if is_truncated and is_exact:
2005 # missing decimals, use computed exact value
2006 need_replace.add(name)
2007 elif is_exact:
2008 exact[name] = val
2009 else:
2010 assert not is_truncated
2011 uncert = float(line[77:99].replace(' ', '').replace('(exact)', '0'))
2012 units = line[99:].rstrip()
2013 constants[name] = (val, units, uncert)
2014 replace = exact_func(exact)
2015 replace_exact(constants, need_replace, replace)
2016 return constants
